slides.title: How long a ladder?
slides.text: The builder needs a ladder to reach the top of a new wall. The wall is 4 meters high, and the ladder's foot must stand 3 meters out. Tally wonders how long the ladder must be.

slides.title: The long side of a right triangle
slides.text: In a right triangle, the square of the long side equals the sum of the squares of the two short sides: a² + b² = c². For the ladder, 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25, and √25 = 5. The ladder is 5 meters long.

visual.label: The wall, the ground and the ladder

focus.cue: The ladder is the long side, across from the square corner.

slides.title: Find a short side
slides.text: A plank ramp is 13 m long and rests on a ledge 5 m high. How far out is its foot? Subtract the squares this time.
steps: The foot is 12 m from the ledge

slides.title: Distance on a grid
slides.text: To find the distance between two points, draw a right triangle under the line between them. Here it goes 3 across and 4 up. Then 3² + 4² = 25, so the points are √25 = 5 units apart.

visual.label: Two towers on the plan grid

focus.cue: 3 across and 4 up make a right triangle under the rope.

slides.title: Checking for a square corner
slides.text: The theorem works backward too. Beams of 6 m, 8 m and 10 m make a square corner, because 6² + 8² = 100 = 10². Beams of 5 m, 6 m and 7 m do not, since 25 + 36 = 61, not 49.

words.means: a triangle with one square corner, an angle of 90°
the long side of a right triangle, across from the square corner
the two shorter sides of a right triangle, which meet at the square corner
the number that, multiplied by itself, gives the number: √25 = 5

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Keep Builder at Ladders and Spans. Find a ladder, a ramp and a rope between two towers, build squares on a triangle's sides and test three beams for a square corner.
slides.alt: Keep Builder on a phone: a wall 4 m high with a ladder leaning on it from 3 m out, and a stepper to set the ladder's length.
